top_cited_works.title: VELOCITY-FIELD MEASUREMENTS OF A SHOCK-ACCELERATED FLUID INSTABILITY
top_cited_works.venue: University of North Texas Digital Library (University of North Texas)
top_cited_works.abstract: A cylinder of heavy gas (SF{sub 6}) in air is hit by a Mach 1.2 shock. The resultant Richtmyer-Meshkov instability is observed as it propagates through the test section of the shock tube. Six images are taken after shock impact, and the velocity field at one time is measured using Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). The images of the density field show the development of a secondary instability in the cylinder. The velocity field provides us with information about the magnitudes of the velocities as well as the magnitude of the vorticity in the flow.

top_cited_works.title: Modeling and Optimization of a Multi-Flow Falling Particle Receiver for Generation 3 Concentrating Solar Power
top_cited_works.abstract: Abstract Generation 3 concentrating solar power (CSP) systems use solid particles for heat transfer and thermal energy storage. Particle-based systems can use a falling particle receiver with an open cavity that allows particles to flow together as a curtain. The particle curtain is directly exposed to solar radiation, which is absorbed by the particles as they descend through the receiver. The efficiency of the particle receiver depends on curtain opacity (which is influenced by the mass flowrate of the particles), the average particle temperature, and environmental factors like wind. This research presents a free-falling particle receiver with optimized particle supply management facilitated by ten individually controlled valves. Each valve is equipped with a slide gate and an actuator, ensuring a consistent mass flowrate for a segment of the curtain. In a uniform mass flowrate curtain, the hottest particles accumulate in the center due to non-uniform flux distribution, which leads to higher radiative and advective losses.
